g.text: Inside one deploy: the single-order scheduler (this branch) against racing evaluation (dev)
a deploy body with parallel branches,
for example
This branch: the single-order scheduler
split the participant into child participants,
each with a causal path (deterministic_reduction.rs:92-133)
each child submits one RSpace intent and waits
complete frontier: every live participant
waits or has completed (:827-841)
native execution adds the key [2, 0] to every footprint,
so each native frontier is one conflict component
What it supplies to cost accounting today
· equal replay host work at live map sizes
(DR-78, DR-79 step 5, DR-100)
· operation names by causal path
(DR-74, DR-84 to DR-86)
· order-dependent decisions without a record
(the G3 design draft)
· checkpoints that never see a partial evaluation
run the intents one at a time, in causal order:
the single order of a native deploy
Dev: racing evaluation
spawn each branch as a Tokio task
and await every handle (dev reduce.rs:318-337)
What a return would need (RD-1 to RD-4)
· RD-1: replay admits operations in journal order
· RD-2: names by RSpace source and occurrence
(a protocol-6 evidence change)
· RD-3: recorded G3 decisions, and settlement
in recorded attempt order
· RD-4: a replay stall verdict, which also fixes
a latent hang of native replay at HEAD
the tasks race: per-channel locks serialize
one channel, and arrival order decides the rest
RSpace picks one matching candidate:
the canonical order at e38ff0de8, and a random pick
after the restoration of dev's pick (dev ops_produce.rs:251-261)
play writes the record: the event log
and the native cost evidence
Dev: "Rholang Is Non-Deterministic By Design"
(docs/rholang-evaluation-order.md:5). Replay
"uses the play event log to force the exact same
COMMs during replay, regardless of evaluation order"
(lines 25-26). Record and replay in §7 works
under both branches of this diagram.
replay follows the record: the recorded COMMs,
whatever the order of the run
colour
meaning
the input: one deploy body
a step of the single-order scheduler of this branch
a step of dev's racing evaluation
the RSpace candidate pick
the record that play writes
replay of the record
what the scheduler supplies today
the record-based designs that a return would need
name
meaning
participant
one live causal branch of a reducer evaluation
intent
a typed request for one RSpace produce or consume
complete frontier
the point at which every live participant waits on one intent or has completed
footprint, [2, 0]
the resources that an intent can touch, and the common key that native execution adds to every footprint
conflict component
a connected component of intents whose footprints intersect
native deploy
an offered (v6) deploy under the native cost meter. Legacy deploys bypass the queue.
COMM
one RSpace communication event: a send that matches a receive
DR-n
decision record n of the cost-accounting decision records
G3
installer funding, a gap of epic 8946 that has no code yet
RD-1 to RD-4
the four record-based designs of the proposal, §3.7.6
HEAD, e38ff0de8
the code basis of the proposal on feature/cost-accounted-rho
dev, a06e3e7b3
the integration branch of F1R3node, at the commit that the dev citations use
